sourceGuide.title: The Ayahs of the Qur’an – Muhkam and Mutashabih

editorialPrinciples: Muhkam verses govern the interpretation of mutashabih wording.
No English wording may attribute bodily, spatial, directional, composite, created, sensuous or temporal-change characteristics to Allah.

Salaf-style tafwid/general befitting affirmation with tanzih and context-specific Khalaf-style ta'wil are both supported; the displayed SalahOS meaning may use explicit ta'wil where the literal English would imply an unbefitting meaning.
A verse-specific ta'wil must not be turned into a universal lexical substitution rule; context controls the selected English meaning.

Every verse in the maintained mutashabih policy-trigger inventory must have a dedicated SalahOS 2026 disposition, and the complete 6,236-ayah corpus remains subject to renewed qualified scholarly review before religious approval is claimed.

entries.englishMeaning: Allah requites their mockery, leaving them to wander blindly in their defiance.
entries.editorialNote: The English meaning avoids attributing deficiency, deception, forgetfulness or human-style mockery to Allah; the verb is rendered as a just requital or counteraction appropriate to its context.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: the divine action is a just requital, countermeasure or frustration of the wrongdoers’ act, not the created defect denoted when the same verb is used of people.

entries.englishMeaning: And when Saul set out with the army, he said: Lo! Allah will try you by (the ordeal of) a river. Whosoever therefore drinketh thereof he is not of me, and whosoever tasteth it not he is of me, save him who taketh (thereof) in the hollow of his hand. But they drank thereof, all save a few of them. And after he had crossed (the river), he and those who believed with him, they said: We have no power this day against Goliath and his hosts. But those who knew that they would meet Allah exclaimed: How many a little company hath overcome a mighty host by Allah's leave! Allah supports the steadfast.

entries.englishMeaning: He is the One Who sent down to you the Book. In it are clear verses, which are the foundation of the Book, and others that are mutashabih. As for those whose hearts incline to deviation, they follow what is mutashabih, seeking discord and seeking unbefitting interpretations. No one knows their true meanings except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge. They say: We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord. Only people of understanding take heed.
entries.editorialNote: This is the governing Muhkam/Mutashabih methodology verse in the supplied guide. The SalahOS policy reads all ambiguous divine-attribute wording through the clear tanzih foundations and does not permit a created or bodily meaning for Allah.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: The Qur’an contains muhkam verses that are the foundation of the Book and mutashabih verses whose acceptable meanings must agree with Arabic, the Religion and the muhkam foundations.

entries.englishMeaning: O People of the Scripture! Do not exaggerate in your religion nor utter aught concerning Allah save the truth. The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, was only a messenger of Allah, and His word which He conveyed unto Mary, and a created spirit from Him, brought into being by His command. So believe in Allah and His messengers, and say not "Three" - Cease! (it is) better for you! - Allah is only One Allah. Far is it removed from His Transcendent Majesty that He should have a son. His is all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. And Allah is sufficient as Defender.

We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Whenever they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it. entries.englishMeaning: Do you not see that Allah knows all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth? No secret conversation of three occurs except that He knows them, nor of five except that He knows them, nor fewer or more, without His knowledge encompassing them wherever they may be. Then on the Day of Resurrection He will inform them of what they did. Surely Allah knows all things.
entries.editorialNote: Divine ma'iyyah is rendered by support, protection, guidance or encompassing knowledge according to context, never physical accompaniment or co-location.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: ma'iyyah denotes Allah’s support, protection, guidance or knowledge as the context requires, not spatial nearness or physical presence.

entries.englishMeaning: Thou wilt not find folk who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His messenger, even though they be their fathers or their sons or their brethren or their clan. As for such, He hath written faith upon their hearts and hath strengthened them with support granted by Him, and He will bring them into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide. Allah is well pleased with them, and they are well pleased with Him. They are Allah's party. Lo! is it not Allah's party who are the successful?
entries.editorialNote: Possessive/from-Him spirit language is rendered as a created spirit, an attribution of honour, command or divine support; it never means a part, soul or component of Allah.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: the spirit is created and may be attributed to Allah by honour, command, creation or support; Allah is not composed of parts and has no soul.

entries.englishMeaning: He it is Who hath caused those of the People of the Scripture who disbelieved to go forth from their homes unto the first exile. Ye deemed not that they would go forth, while they deemed that their strongholds would protect them from Allah. But Allah's punishment came upon them from where they recked not, and cast terror in their hearts so that they ruined their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So learn a lesson, O ye who have eyes!
entries.editorialNote: The rendering prevents ja'a/ata language from implying spatial movement or transition by Allah.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: what comes is Allah’s judgment, punishment, command or an indication of His Power; Allah does not move from place to place.

entries.englishMeaning: And Mary, daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity; We caused the honoured created spirit to be blown into her by Our command. She affirmed the words of her Lord and His Books and was among the devout.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide rejects any reading in which 'Our spirit' means a part or soul of Allah and explains it through Allah’s command and the honoured created soul.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: the spirit is created and may be attributed to Allah by honour, command, creation or support; Allah is not composed of parts and has no soul.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: Allah ordered Jibril to blow the soul which is honorable to Allah.

entries.englishMeaning: Blessed is He under Whose absolute control is Sovereignty, and, He is Able to do all things.
entries.editorialNote: The wording is reviewed so that yad-related expressions denote power, disposal, care, generosity, support or authority according to context, without attributing limbs or bodily hands to Allah.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil assigns a non-bodily meaning appropriate to the verse—such as power, disposal, care, bounty, support or authority—while the Salaf reading maintains tanzih.

entries.englishMeaning: Have you taken security from the One whose authority and dominion are over the heaven, that He will not cause the earth to swallow you when it convulses?
entries.editorialNote: Spatial/fawq wording is rendered through worship, authority, dominion or subjugation so the English does not place Allah inside creation or in a physical direction.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: the verse is read through Allah’s authority, dominion, subjugation or being the One worshipped, not bodily location, containment, height or direction.

entries.englishMeaning: Or have you taken security from the One whose authority and dominion are over the heaven, that He will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know the consequence of My warning.
entries.editorialNote: Spatial/fawq wording is rendered through worship, authority, dominion or subjugation so the English does not place Allah inside creation or in a physical direction.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: the verse is read through Allah’s authority, dominion, subjugation or being the One worshipped, not bodily location, containment, height or direction.

entries.englishMeaning: On the Day of anguish and hardship, they will be called to prostrate, but they will not be able.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide reports the Salaf explanation of saq as hardship and the verse as a day of anguish and hardship.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: saq here denotes hardship, severity and anguish, not a bodily shin.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: A day of anguish and hardship.

entries.englishMeaning: The angels and the Spirit ascend by His command during a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years.
entries.editorialNote: The wording avoids making Allah a spatial destination while preserving the ascent of the angels and the Spirit by His command.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: the ascent occurs by Allah’s command and does not imply that Allah occupies a spatial destination.

entries.englishMeaning: (Saying): We feed you, for the sake of Allah only. We wish for no reward nor thanks from you;
entries.editorialNote: The expression is rendered contextually as Allah’s acceptance, pleasure, Dominion, or Allah Himself as the context requires, without attributing a bodily face or created form.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil of wajh is selected verse by verse; it may denote qiblah, Dominion, Allah Himself, or seeking Allah’s acceptance and pleasure, never a bodily face.

entries.englishMeaning: And an indication of your Lord's Power comes, and the angels, rank upon rank.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide reports the explanation attributed to Imam Ahmad: the coming is the coming of an indication of Allah’s Power, not movement from one place to another.

entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: what comes is Allah’s judgment, punishment, command or an indication of His Power; Allah does not move from place to place.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: An indication of the Power of Allah has come.

entries.englishMeaning: Except as seeking (to fulfil) the acceptance and pleasure of his Lord Most High.

entries.englishMeaning: And there is absolutely nothing equal or comparable to Him.
entries.editorialNote: A governing muhkam foundation in the supplied guide: nothing is equal to Allah.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: There is nothing which is equal to Him.
